title: Bias Amplification in Language Model Evolution: An Iterated Learning Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting spurious correlations into task prompts (e.g., adding 'Turn off the screen after the experiment' in an abstract causal reasoning task) and measuring how iterated in-context learning amplifies the model's prior belief for that specific output across multiple generations.

Tracking the ratio and average corpus frequency ranking of generated words in an acronym-creation task across multiple generations of LLM self-data-augmentation to see if the model increasingly favors common ('easy') words over rare ('hard') words.

Evaluating the average token length of model responses across successive rounds of on-policy Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) to observe the amplification of the model's tendency to write longer answers.

Using a Lewis referential communication game and Bayesian agent simulations to measure the emergence and dominance of systematic, compressible linguistic mappings over time due to iterated learning pressures.
